summary:
Space Graveyard is an interactive digital narrative that reactivates abandoned and inactive machinery on the Moon and Mars. Using story, users can learn about what each of these spacecrafts achieved, why it was abandoned, and the science that came out of the discovery.
Space Graveyard brings to life the legacy of abandoned machinery. The machines, which could otherwise be seen as nothing more than space junk, are instead presented as a record of human curiosity, failures, and discovery. Space Graveyard is created to engage young space fans in mission history.
Why does it matter? Because the discoveries made by these machines inform our understanding of the moon, Mars, and space travel in the future.
details:
The Space Graveyard is a digital human centred museum made for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. This museum showcases the stories of human made machines that have been left on the moon and mars.

There are 5 artifacts included in this project; the Apollo 11 Descent Stage, Sojourner Rover, Pathfinder Lander, Opportunity Rover and Lunar Laser Retroreflector. Each has their own museum style profile containing information about what they are, what missions they did, what they achieved and what their legacy is.

This website includes an interactive map of the moon and mars showing where historic landings happened, a timeline showing the major milestones in space exploration from 1969-2019, images and schematics of the artifacts and a quiz containing 10 questions to test your knowledge. This quiz contains explanations to each question instantly and keeps track of your highest score.

This project is aimed at students aged between 10 and 18 years old. The main aim is to create a new perspective on the abandoned equipment in space. We want to educate younger people on the scientific importance of these pieces of equipment and the hard work put into every mission. We want to show that there is a big difference between equipment that has been left behind and equipment that is still contributing to science.

This project was created using 9 pages in React. Using local storage in the browser to keep track of quiz scores, bespoke vector schematics and images from NASA (public domain). We researched using NASA Science, Planetary Data System, Jet Propulsion Laboratory mission logs, Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter images and NASA Lunar Laser Ranging information.

This project was very creative as we used a museum style approach to educating people about space. This combines stories, historic images, interactive maps, timelines and quizzes.

We considered the scientific accuracy of the information, the age of our audience, clear visuals, accessibility and the difference between equipment that isn’t contributing and equipment that is still contributing to science. We wanted to inspire students to become interested in planetary science and show that there is still a story behind every space mission.
